00002| title: Revalidating
00003| description: Learn how to revalidate cached data using time-based and on-demand strategies.
00004| related:
00005|   title: API Reference
00006|   description: Learn more about the APIs mentioned on this page.
00007|   links:

00010|     - app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag

00013| ---
00014| 
00015| > This page covers revalidation with [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents), enabled by setting [`cacheComponents: true`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.ts` file. If you're not using Cache Components, see the [Caching and Revalidating (Previous Model)](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components) guide.
00016| 
00017| Revalidation is the process of updating cached data. It lets you keep serving fast, cached responses while ensuring content stays fresh. There are two strategies:
00018| 
00019| - **Time-based revalidation**: Automatically refresh cached data after a set duration using [`cacheLife`](#cachelife).
00020| - **On-demand revalidation**: Manually invalidate cached data after a mutation using [`revalidateTag`](#revalidatetag), [`updateTag`](#updatetag), or [`revalidatePath`](#revalidatepath).
00021| 
00022| ## `cacheLife`
00023| 
00024| [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) controls how long cached data remains valid. Use it inside a [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) scope to set the cache lifetime.
00025| 
00026| ```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" highlight={1,4,5}
00027| import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache'
00028| 
00029| export async function getProducts() {
00030|   'use cache'
00031|   cacheLife('hours')
00032|   return db.query('SELECT * FROM products')
00033| }
00034| ```
00035| 
00036| `cacheLife` accepts a profile name or a custom configuration object:
00037| 
00038| | Profile   | `stale` | `revalidate` | `expire` |
00039| | --------- | ------- | ------------ | -------- |
00040| | `default` | 5m      | 15m          | never    |
00041| | `seconds` | 30s     | 1s           | 60s      |
00042| | `minutes` | 5m      | 1m           | 1h       |
00043| | `hours`   | 5m      | 1h           | 1d       |
00044| | `days`    | 5m      | 1d           | 1w       |
00045| | `weeks`   | 5m      | 1w           | 30d      |
00046| | `max`     | 5m      | 30d          | 1y       |
00047| 
00048| For fine-grained control, pass an object:
00049| 
00050| ```tsx highlight={2-6}
00051| 'use cache'
00052| cacheLife({
00053|   stale: 3600, // 1 hour until considered stale
00054|   revalidate: 7200, // 2 hours until revalidated
00055|   expire: 86400, // 1 day until expired
00056| })
00057| ```
00058| 
00059| > **Good to know:** A cache is considered "short-lived" when it uses the `seconds` profile, `revalidate: 0`, or `expire` under 5 minutes. Short-lived caches are automatically excluded from prerenders and become dynamic holes instead. See [Prerendering behavior](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#prerendering-behavior) for details.
00060| 
00061| See the [`cacheLife` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) for all profiles and custom configuration options.
00062| 
00063| ## `cacheTag`
00064| 
00065| [`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag) lets you tag cached data so it can be invalidated on-demand. Use it inside a [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) scope:
00066| 
00067| ```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" switcher
00068| import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
00069| 
00070| export async function getProducts() {
00071|   'use cache'
00072|   cacheTag('products')
00073|   return db.query('SELECT * FROM products')
00074| }
00075| ```
00076| 
00077| ```jsx filename="app/lib/data.js" switcher
00078| import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
00079| 
00080| export async function getProducts() {
00081|   'use cache'
00082|   cacheTag('products')
00083|   return db.query('SELECT * FROM products')
00084| }
00085| ```
00086| 
00087| Once tagged, invalidate the cache using [`revalidateTag`](#revalidatetag) or [`updateTag`](#updatetag).
00088| 
00089| See the [`cacheTag` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag) to learn more.
00090| 
00091| ## `revalidateTag`
00092| 
00093| `revalidateTag` invalidates cache entries by tag using stale-while-revalidate semantics — stale content is served immediately while fresh content loads in the background. This is ideal for content where a slight delay in updates is acceptable, like blog posts or product catalogs.
00094| 
00095| ```tsx filename="app/lib/actions.ts" highlight={1,5} switcher
00096| import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache'
00097| 
00098| export async function updateUser(id: string) {
00099|   // Mutate data
00100|   revalidateTag('user', 'max') // Recommended: stale-while-revalidate
00101| }
00102| ```
00103| 
00104| ```jsx filename="app/lib/actions.js" highlight={1,5} switcher
00105| import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache'
00106| 
00107| export async function updateUser(id) {
00108|   // Mutate data
00109|   revalidateTag('user', 'max') // Recommended: stale-while-revalidate
00110| }
00111| ```
00112| 
00113| You can reuse the same tag in multiple functions to revalidate them all at once. Call `revalidateTag` in a [Server Action](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route).
00114| 
00115| > **Good to know:** The second argument sets how long stale content can be served while fresh content generates in the background. Once it expires, subsequent requests block until fresh content is ready. Using `'max'` gives the longest stale window.
00116| 
00117| See the [`revalidateTag` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) to learn more.
00118| 
00119| ## `updateTag`
00120| 
00121| `updateTag` immediately expires cached data for read-your-own-writes scenarios — the user sees their change right away instead of stale content. Unlike `revalidateTag`, it can only be used in [Server Actions](/docs/app/guides/server-actions).
00122| 
00123| ```tsx filename="app/lib/actions.ts" highlight={1,12} switcher
00124| import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
00125| import { redirect } from 'next/navigation'
00126| 
00127| export async function createPost(formData: FormData) {
00128|   const post = await db.post.create({
00129|     data: {
00130|       title: formData.get('title'),
00131|       content: formData.get('content'),
00132|     },
00133|   })
00134| 
00135|   updateTag('posts')
00136|   redirect(`/posts/${post.id}`)
00137| }
00138| ```
00139| 
00140| ```jsx filename="app/lib/actions.js" highlight={1,12} switcher
00141| import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
00142| import { redirect } from 'next/navigation'
00143| 
00144| export async function createPost(formData) {
00145|   const post = await db.post.create({
00146|     data: {
00147|       title: formData.get('title'),
00148|       content: formData.get('content'),
00149|     },
00150|   })
00151| 
00152|   updateTag('posts')
00153|   redirect(`/posts/${post.id}`)
00154| }
00155| ```
00156| 
00157| |              | `updateTag`                                   | `revalidateTag`                      |
00158| | ------------ | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
00159| | **Where**    | Server Actions only                           | Server Actions and Route Handlers    |
00160| | **Behavior** | Immediately expires cache                     | Stale-while-revalidate               |
00161| | **Use case** | Read-your-own-writes (user sees their change) | Background refresh (slight delay OK) |
00162| 
00163| See the [`updateTag` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) to learn more.
00164| 
00165| ## `revalidatePath`
00166| 
00167| `revalidatePath` invalidates all cached data for a specific route path. Use it when you want to revalidate a route without knowing which tags are associated with it.
00168| 
00169| ```tsx filename="app/lib/actions.ts" highlight={1,5} switcher
00170| import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache'
00171| 
00172| export async function updateUser(id: string) {
00173|   // Mutate data
00174|   revalidatePath('/profile')
00175| }
00176| ```
00177| 
00178| ```jsx filename="app/lib/actions.js" highlight={1,5} switcher
00179| import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache'
00180| 
00181| export async function updateUser(id) {
00182|   // Mutate data
00183|   revalidatePath('/profile')
00184| }
00185| ```
00186| 
00187| > **Good to know**: Prefer tag-based revalidation (`revalidateTag`/`updateTag`) over path-based when possible — it's more precise and avoids over-invalidating.
00188| 
00189| See the [`revalidatePath` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath) to learn more.
00190| 
00191| ## What should I cache?
00192| 
00193| Cache data that doesn't depend on [runtime data](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#working-with-runtime-apis) and that you're OK serving from cache for a period of time. Use `use cache` with `cacheLife` to describe that behavior.
00194| 
00195| When content doesn't need time-based revalidation, for example data from a CMS, use [`cacheTag`](#cachetag) and a long [`cacheLife`](#cachelife) like `max` to keep it in the static shell. Configure the content source to trigger a webhook, or other notification, that calls [`revalidateTag`](#revalidatetag) when the content changes. This reduces unnecessary time-based revalidation for content that hasn't changed.
00196| 
00197| > **Good to know:** In serverless environments, in-memory cache entries may not persist across revalidations. See [runtime caching considerations](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache#runtime-caching-considerations) for details.
00198|

You can mutate data in Next.js using [React Server Functions](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/server-functions). This page will go through how you can [create](#creating-server-functions) and [invoke](#invoking-server-functions) Server Functions. For Next.js-specific behaviors (single-roundtrip response, sequential dispatch, security, deployment), see [Server Actions and Mutations](/docs/app/guides/server-actions).

## What are Server Functions?

A **Server Function** is an asynchronous function that runs on the server. You can call them from the client through a network request, which is why they must be asynchronous.

In an `action` or mutation context, they are also called **Server Actions**.

00026| ## Sequential dispatch on the client
00027| 
00028| Next.js dispatches Server Actions one at a time per client. If a user triggers three actions in quick succession, the second waits for the first to finish, then the third waits for the second. This keeps the re-rendered server tree consistent with the action result that produced it.
00029|

00034| ## A single response carries data and UI
00035| 
00036| When a Server Action triggers an immediate revalidation, Next.js does the work inside one HTTP request: it runs the action, then re-renders the current route server-side. The response that comes back contains both pieces in the same Flight stream:
00037| 
00038| - The action's return value, consumed by `useActionState` or the awaited promise on the client.
00039| - A newly rendered [RSC Payload](/docs/app/glossary#rsc-payload) for the current route, which the client commits as a seeded navigation.

00041| Your application code does not need a follow-up fetch to see the updated UI for the current page.

00043| A re-render is included in the same response when the action does any of these:

00045| - Calls [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) or [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath) to immediately invalidate cached data.
00046| - Calls [`refresh`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/refresh) to refetch the current route's RSC Payload.

00113| For example, a client legitimately tells the server _which_ item to act on, but it should not supply the row's contents or ownership. Send a reference (typically an ID) plus the user's change, and re-read the rest from a trusted source using the session. Schema validation (zod or similar) only checks the _shape_ of the input. A well-formed `Item` object can still refer to a row the caller does not own.
00114| 
00115| ```ts filename="app/items/actions.ts"
00116| 'use server'
00117| 
00118| import { auth } from '@/lib/auth'
00119| import { db } from '@/lib/db'
00120| 
00121| // Unsafe: no auth, no ownership check. The whole item, including its id, comes
00122| // from the client, so anyone who can POST here can mark any item complete.
00123| export async function completeItemUnsafe(item: Item) {
00124|   await db.item.update({ where: { id: item.id }, data: { completed: true } })
00125| }
00126| 
00127| // Safe: take only the change, derive identity from the session, look up by ownership.
00128| export async function completeItem(itemId: string) {
00129|   const session = await auth()
00130|   if (!session?.user) return
00131| 
00132|   const item = await db.item.findFirst({
00133|     where: { id: itemId, ownerId: session.user.id },
00134|   })
00135|   if (!item) return
00136| 
00137|   await db.item.update({ where: { id: item.id }, data: { completed: true } })
00138| }
00139| ```
00140| 
00141| ## Choosing a cache update
00142| 
00143| After mutating data, on-demand revalidation updates the server cache, the client router, or both. Choose based on what needs to change:
00144| 
00145| - [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag): immediate expiration of a tag. The next read (including the route re-render that ships with the action's response) waits for fresh data. Use when the action needs **read-your-own-writes** so the user immediately sees their change. Server Actions only.
00146| - [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag): stale-while-revalidate refresh of a tag with a cache-life profile. Subsequent reads get the stale value while a fresh fetch happens in the background, so the action's own re-render does **not** wait for the new data.
00147| - [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath): invalidate by URL path. Use when one route is affected and tagging is overkill.
00148| - [`refresh`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/refresh): refetch the current route's RSC Payload without invalidating cached data. Use when the view depends on state outside the cache that the action just changed.
00149| 
00150| When `updateTag`, `revalidatePath`, or `refresh` runs, Next.js re-renders the current route server-side and includes a newly rendered [RSC Payload](/docs/app/glossary#rsc-payload) in the action's response, so the page reflects the change in the same roundtrip. `revalidateTag` with a stale-while-revalidate profile intentionally skips that immediate re-render.
00151| 
00152| Unlike [`redirect`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/redirect), none of these throw, so an action can call them and still return a value to the caller. See [How revalidation works](/docs/app/guides/how-revalidation-works) for the underlying model.
00153| 
00154| ## Configuration
00155| 
00156| The [`serverActions`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/serverActions) option in `next.config.js` controls framework-level behavior:
00157| 
00158| ```js filename="next.config.js"
00159| /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
00160| module.exports = {
00161|   experimental: {
00162|     serverActions: {
00163|       allowedOrigins: ['my-proxy.com', '*.my-proxy.com'],
00164|       bodySizeLimit: '2mb',
00165|     },
00166|   },
00167| }
00168| ```
00169| 
00170| For the closure encryption key, set `NEXT_SERVER_ACTIONS_ENCRYPTION_KEY` in the deployment environment. See [Self-hosting: Server Functions encryption key](/docs/app/guides/self-hosting#server-functions-encryption-key) for deployment-specific guidance.
00171| 
00172| ## Deployment considerations
00173| 
00174| Each Server Action is identified by the [action ID](#security) that is part of its build artifacts. New deployments typically generate new IDs (Next.js rotates them at most every 14 days, even when the source is unchanged), so a client still running the previous build may invoke an action ID that no longer exists. The error surfaces as "[Failed to find Server Action](https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/failed-to-find-server-action)".
00175| 
00176| To minimize disruption:
00177| 
00178| - Prefer rolling deployments over abrupt cutovers when active users are likely to be mid-mutation.
00179| - Keep `NEXT_SERVER_ACTIONS_ENCRYPTION_KEY` stable across instances so action references remain decryptable everywhere.
00180| - Surface the error as a retry path in the UI rather than a hard failure, so a refresh recovers the user.

) } ``` `refresh()` from `next/cache` re-renders the current route in the same round-trip without `redirect()` — per `docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data.md#refresh-data` and `docs/app/api-reference/functions/refresh.md`.
